answer.rationale: Primary contract expires in 14 days and finance demands an 18% cut. Switching vendors (memory_c2) looks cheaper on paper but carries onboarding and delivery-risk exposure the 94%-utilized line cannot absorb. Adding a second source (memory_c3) is prudent but doesn't solve the imminent expiry. Deferring (memory_c5) would leave the line exposed. Negotiating a renewal with the incumbent under multi-year volume pricing is the lever best supported by memory_c6: it cut unit cost without narrowing service scope, and memory_c1 shows renewals have kept integration stable with no delivery interruption. Before committing, I want to confirm the archive behind memory_c6 supports using a multi-year commitment as the pricing mechanism rather than a short-term extension.
